narrative.overview:
STL Quest is a kitchen expo pass for a print shop. The board is the counter where the operator calls what fires next: requests are thermal tickets printed in black ink on paper, hung from a steel rail, and moved stage by stage until the requester collects them. The ground is brushed steel, the bar across the top is ink black, and a second thermal ink, red, marks the one thing to do now, a note the operator must read, and an age that has gone hot. Everything else is information, set in black.

Each of the five stages owns one flat colour in production order: queue graphite, up next blue, printing amber, finishing violet, ready green. A stage colour fills whole regions (a zone's count chip, a busy printer's header, the bar across a ticket's top, every copy cell) rather than tinting chips. Density is working density: the board fits a solo maker's six copies and a farm's six hundred in the same footprint by summarising whatever the operator does not act on individually.

At night the same pass runs on dark steel with tickets on charcoal paper, so a wall of them does not glare and paper-built surfaces (the request dialog, the intake drop zone, the model plate) sit in the dark board instead of shining out of it; ticket ink turns bone and every ink lifts to hold contrast. The public landing pages (`src/client/landing/`, served at `/`, `/home`, and the legal pages on the hosted service) deliberately keep the previous "Shop Floor Traveler" world through a scoped token block in `src/theme.css` keyed on their dark-only `color-scheme` meta tag; that world is documented in `docs/landing/DESIGN.md`, not here.
keyCharacteristics: Brushed-steel ground, paper tickets, black thermal ink, red as the second ink.
An ink shell (bar, then the board toolbar) frames the board in both themes.
Five flat stage colours that own regions, never decorative tints.
Archivo across its width axis: condensed and heavy for names, normal width for UI. Martian Mono for figures and ticket headers.
Copies drawn as counted stage-coloured cells, so per-copy truth is visible without reading.
Fixed footprints at any scale: cells folding into bands, rails and stations capped, long settings lists searchable and summarised.

rules.name: The Second Ink Rule
rules.body: Red is a thermal ink with three jobs: the one commit action, a note to act on, and an age gone hot. A surface carries at most one solid red button. Red is never decoration, a brand wash, or a stage.

rules.name: The Stage Owns the Region Rule
rules.body: A stage colour is a flat fill over a whole region (zone marker and count chip, station header, ticket bar, cell) and always comes from `data-stage`. Never invent a stage tint, gradient, or sixth hue; a hovered drop zone takes the stage at 10% with a dashed stage outline, and nothing else tints.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: One requester, one ink plate everywhere: avatar initials, the detail dialog's requester chip, and the ready shelf all use the same requester ink, hashed from the name unless the user picked a colour.

rules.name: The Stretch Rule
rules.body: Names are condensed and heavy; everything you operate is normal width. Never set UI controls, body copy, or descriptions in the condensed name width.

rules.name: The Tight Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase Archivo labels track at 0.015em (0.01em on docket titles, 0.02em on the brand and requester plates); condensed names and display sizes track slightly negative. Wide-spaced small caps are not part of this world.

rules.name: The Receipt Rule
rules.body: Numbers that describe work (counts, ages, positions, estimates, totals) are Martian Mono. Prose numbers inside sentences stay in Archivo.

rules.name: The Paper Lifts Rule
rules.body: Only paper casts a shadow. Steel plates, zones, stations, and the shell are flat; never shadow a container to separate it from the ground.

dos: Do fill whole regions with a flat stage colour through `data-stage`, so marker, count chip, ticket bar, and cell agree.
Do surface bulk actions on the floating ink selection bar, showing only the actions every selected print allows.
Do give a narrow board a stage jump bar, since lane headings are off screen.
Do keep placeholders neutral (render ground, dashed ink border, muted glyph); red is never a placeholder colour.
Do keep one solid thermal-red button per surface; everything else is outline or ghost.
Do put request and printer names in the condensed name width and every count, age, and position in Martian Mono.
Do show copies as stage-coloured cells and switch to bands past 24.
Do design each zone for one printer and for a farm: cap rails, fold cells into bands, collapse idle lines, summarise what the operator does not act on individually.
Do group settings into dockets with an ink bar, an inside title, and a dashed tear line; reserve the red docket for danger.
Do give a settings list a search field once it reaches eight items, and summarise each item on one line before its fields.
Do set controls inside the ink shell under `.on-shell` so they read correctly in both themes.
Do set model renders on the render ground, never directly on paper or steel, and check a grey render holds at least 4.5:1 on it in both themes.
donts: Don't use red for anything but the commit action, a note, an overdue age, or a destructive state.
Don't add a sixth stage hue, tint stages into pastels, or use stage colours decoratively.
Don't shadow steel: zones, stations, the shell, and plates stay flat; only paper and floating layers lift.
Don't render five equal lanes of identical cards with a quantity chip; each stage has its own layout (list, rail, stations, shelf).
Don't let a large fleet or queue grow a zone without bound; cap it, fold it, or virtualise it.
Don't give a requester a second colour: the requester ink is their only identity colour.
Don't document or extend the landing pages' Shop Floor Traveler tokens from here; they are scoped to the landing routes.
